claims.sentence: On 23 September 2026 the WHO published guidelines on expanding contraceptive options, covering extended pill use, longer implant use and an extra emergency option.
claims.evidence: WHO news item dated 23-09-2026 'WHO expands safe options for contraception'; covers extended pills, implants, mifepristone.

claims.sentence: The WHO released its guidelines on expanding contraceptive options on 23 September 2026.
The guidelines support extended use of combined oral contraceptive pills as an alternative to cyclical use.
claims.evidence: Combined pills used extended as alternative to cyclical use, up to six months or continuously up to one year.

claims.sentence: They also support longer use of contraceptive implants and add mifepristone as an emergency contraception option.
claims.evidence: Implants supported for up to five years; mifepristone recommended as additional emergency contraception option.

claims.sentence: The WHO recommends against adding quinestrol-containing contraceptive pills to national programmes.
claims.evidence: 'recommends against adding quinestrol-containing contraceptive pills to national contraceptive programmes'.

claims.sentence: The World Health Organization (WHO) published "WHO guidelines on expanding contraceptive options" on 23 September 2026.
claims.evidence: Guideline titled 'WHO guidelines on expanding contraceptive options'; news dated 23 September 2026.

claims.sentence: The WHO now supports extended use of combined oral contraceptive pills as an alternative to cyclical use, and longer use of contraceptive implants, which it says may reduce the need for replacement procedures, clinic visits and costs.
claims.evidence: Extended pill use alternative to cyclical use; implants up to five years, 'potentially reducing the need for replacement procedures, clinic visits and associated costs'.

claims.sentence: Mifepristone is recommended as an additional emergency contraception option.
claims.evidence: 'recommends mifepristone as an additional emergency contraception option', within five days of unprotected sex, doses 10-50 mg.

claims.sentence: The WHO recommends against adding quinestrol-containing contraceptive pills to national contraceptive programmes, and says more research is needed on ormeloxifene before it enters family planning programmes.
claims.evidence: Quinestrol recommended against; 'more research around ormeloxifene before inclusion in family planning programs'.

claims.sentence: The WHO also published its first Target Product Profile for male contraceptive methods, which sets out what such products would need to achieve.
claims.evidence: News item says WHO developed its first Target Product Profile for male contraceptives (safety, effectiveness, acceptability, affordability). Document was a public-review draft dated 20 Feb 2026; 'published' on 23 Sept is not confirmed.
claims.newSentence: The WHO also announced its first Target Product Profile for male contraceptive methods, which sets out what such products would need to achieve.

claims.sentence: The WHO frames the new guidelines as widening the safe options available to people choosing a method.
claims.evidence: Headline 'WHO expands safe options for contraception'.

notes: TPP for male contraceptives: draft for public review dated 20 Feb 2026 (cdn.who.int tpp-male-contraceptives-for-public-review.pdf); contraception topic page lists a 22 Sept 2026 entry; news 23 Sept. Reworded c10 to 'announced' to avoid claiming a publication date. Brief says 'WHO guidelines' date 23 Sept 2026 which matches the news item; the IRIS handle 10665/387579 appeared for the guideline. Did not open full guideline text.
